'''Attila Endre Pavlath''' (March 11,  1930  – November 22, 2024) was a [[Hungarian Americans|Hungarian-American]] chemist. He served as president of the [[American Chemical Society]].

== Life ==

He was born on March 11,  1930 in [[Budapest]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://cen.acs.org/people/obituaries/Obituary-Attila-E-Pavlath/103/web/2025/02|title=Obituary: Attila E. Pavlath|first=Sara|last=Cottle|date=21 January 2025|website=Chemical & Engineering News}}</ref>

He married and had two children: Grace and George.<ref name="auto"/>

He died on November 22, 2024 in [[Atlanta]].<ref name="auto"/>

== Education ==

He completed his diploma in chemical engineering at the [[Budapest University of Technology and Economics|Technical University of Budapest]].<ref name="auto"/>

He earned his PhD in chemistry from the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="auto"/>

== Career  ==

=== Academic ===

He accepted a research fellow position at [[McGill University]] in 1956.<ref name="auto"/>

He was a member of the Royal Society of Great Britain.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/science-legacy-attila-pavlath-121920917.html?guccounter=1&guce_referrer=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ29vZ2xlLmNvbS8&guce_referrer_sig=AQAAACXUsJupf0YVM8gKxG-AFeNVP-BVkKejQPzM0y8azogyI1I2aKCwQCuiiTTJvp78zuDOMTIH5XYjSbs5baDPP_snKj1j7rA5uZ4T1iWLr8meD70MmPur4WKA47W5bdEMYi2W97hrf9_gmMWwNbd0LhreaoUyrZiC4bVUyLTCRBsn|title=Science and Legacy of Attila Pavlath}}</ref>

=== Practical ===

He served as senior emeritus scientist at the [[U.S. Department of Agriculture]] (USDA).<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.jennystanford.com/author/attila-pavlath/|title=Attila Pavlath}}</ref>

In 1958, he joined [[Stauffer Chemical Company]] of California where he led a research group on agricultural problems.<ref name="auto1"/>

He served as president of the [[American Chemical Society]].<ref name="auto"/>

== Recognition ==

* [[Charles Lathrop Parsons Award]] of [[American Chemical Society]] (2019)<ref name="auto"/>
* Kenneth A. Spencer Award for Outstanding Achievement in Agricultural and Food Chemistry from the ACS Kansas City Section (2013).<ref name="auto"/>

== Bibliography ==

He has published more than 130 research papers, he has authored 10 books and several chapters, and he also holds 25 patents.<ref name="auto1"/>
